learning.def: A relatively lasting change in behavior or knowledge that comes from experience.

behaviorism.def: The view that psychology should study observable behavior and how the environment shapes it, setting aside inner mental states that cannot be observed.

classical-conditioning.def: Learning in which a neutral stimulus, after being paired with a stimulus that already triggers a response, comes to trigger a similar response on its own. Also called Pavlovian conditioning.

neutral-stimulus.def: A stimulus that, before conditioning, does not trigger the response being studied (a tone before it is paired with food).

ucs.def: Unconditioned stimulus (UCS): a stimulus that triggers a response naturally, with no learning (food, a puff of air, a loud noise).

ucr.def: Unconditioned response (UCR): the unlearned, automatic response to the unconditioned stimulus (salivating to food).

cs.def: Conditioned stimulus (CS): a once-neutral stimulus that, after pairing with the UCS, triggers a learned response on its own.

cr.def: Conditioned response (CR): the learned response to the conditioned stimulus (salivating to the tone).

acquisition.def: The first stage of conditioning, when the neutral stimulus is paired with the UCS and the link to the response is learned.

extinction.def: The weakening of a conditioned response when the CS is repeatedly presented without the UCS.

spontaneous-recovery.def: The return of an extinguished conditioned response after a rest period, usually weaker than before.

stimulus-discrimination.def: Learning to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli that were never paired with the UCS.

stimulus-generalization.def: The tendency for stimuli similar to the conditioned stimulus to trigger the conditioned response too.

higher-order.def: Higher-order (second-order) conditioning: pairing a new neutral stimulus with an established CS, so the new stimulus also comes to trigger the CR without the UCS ever being present.

counterconditioning.def: Pairing a conditioned stimulus with a new stimulus that triggers a response incompatible with the old CR (calm instead of fear), so the new response replaces the old one.

taste-aversion.def: A learned dislike of a food or taste after it was followed by illness. It can form after a single pairing, even with hours between the taste and the illness.

preparedness.def: Biological preparedness: an inborn readiness, shaped by natural selection, to learn some associations (taste with illness, fear of snakes) faster and more lastingly than others.

habituation.def: A decrease in response to a stimulus that is repeated without any consequence. The simplest form of learning; it needs no pairing.
